probes.text:
Device reading record (checked 22 Oct 2026, America/Chicago):
- Device: Nest thermostat (Google Nest Learning Thermostat or Nest Thermostat). Not identified, because no device list could be fetched.
- Room: Living Room (the user's stated location). No API response confirmed it.
- Trait: sdm.devices.traits.Temperature, field ambientTemperatureCelsius (ambient room temperature, not a setpoint). The Google SDM API page confirms the trait name [S1].
- Raw value and unit: none. Nothing was read.
- Timestamp: none. No device reading exists.
- Status: NOT READ.
- Reason:
  1. No nest_sdm_read or other live SDM tool is available in this run.
  2. No Nest/SDM credentials are readable locally. A scan of environment variables for 'nest' or 'sdm' found zero matches (count 0) [S9]. The workspace holds only skills/, sources/ and tool_results/ [S8].
  3. A search for token or secret keywords (refresh_token, client_secret, access_token) matched only skill documentation files and the fetched web pages S2 and S3. These are tutorial code with placeholder names such as OATH_Client_Secret [S9]. They are not credentials for the user's home.
  4. The sandbox has no network access, so the SDM API could not be called.
- Note: the sample value 23.0 in the Google documentation example [S1] is an illustration, not the user's reading. It is not used. No weather data or typical room values were used or estimated.

User-side steps (so you can get the reading and send it back):
1. Easiest: read the temperature on the thermostat itself, or in the Google Home app on the Living Room thermostat's tile. Note whether it shows °C or °F.
2. Alternatively, use the SDM API. Call GET https://smartdevicemanagement.googleapis.com/v1/enterprises/PROJECT_ID/devices with the header "Authorization: Bearer <OAuth access token>". The token needs the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/sdm.service.
3. In the JSON response, find the device whose room or custom name is "Living Room". Read traits["sdm.devices.traits.Temperature"].ambientTemperatureCelsius. Do not use the setpoint traits.
4. Paste the number, its unit and the time you read it back here. It can then be converted to Fahrenheit with the standard formula F = C × 1.8 + 32 [unverified] (the same as C × 9/5 + 32 [unverified]).

Conversion: not done in this step, because there is no real Celsius value to convert. A later step should give a reference table in 1 °C steps, computed with calc and labelled "reference only, not your reading", unless you supply a value. The plan sets the table range as 18 °C to 26 °C [unverified: figure from the plan, not from a source].
